title: Filter a total
prompt: Using a subquery in FROM, show the order_id and units of orders with more than 3 total units. Replace the ___.
hints: The outer query can use the inner query's columns.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT order_id, units FROM (SELECT order_id, SUM(quantity) AS units FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id) WHERE units > 3;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT order_id, units FROM (SELECT order_id, SUM(quantity) AS units FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id);
SELECT order_id, quantity AS units FROM order_items WHERE quantity > 3;

title: Average of averages
prompt: Show the average of each department's average salary, rounded to 2 decimals, as avg_of_avgs. Ignore employees with no department.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT ROUND(AVG(avg_salary), 2) AS avg_of_avgs FROM (SELECT AVG(salary) AS avg_salary FROM employees WHERE department_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY department_id);

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(salary), 2) AS avg_of_avgs FROM employees WHERE department_id IS NOT NULL;
SELECT ROUND(AVG(avg_salary), 2) AS avg_of_avgs FROM (SELECT AVG(salary) AS avg_salary FROM employees GROUP BY department_id);

title: Biggest customer
prompt: Show the customer_id with the most orders and that count as orders. Break ties with the lowest customer_id.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT customer_id, orders FROM (SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id) ORDER BY orders DESC, customer_id LIMIT 1;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT customer_id, orders FROM (SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id) ORDER BY orders, customer_id LIMIT 1;
SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders;

title: Joined summary
prompt: Show each student's name and average grade as average, rounded to 1 decimal, by joining students to a subquery of averages.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring');

solutions: SELECT s.name, a.average FROM students s JOIN (SELECT student_id, ROUND(AVG(grade), 1) AS average FROM enrolments GROUP BY student_id) a ON a.student_id = s.id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT s.name, a.average FROM students s JOIN (SELECT student_id, ROUND(AVG(grade), 1) AS average FROM enrolments GROUP BY student_id) a ON a.student_id = s.year_group;
SELECT s.name, ROUND(MAX(e.grade), 1) AS average FROM students s JOIN enrolments e ON e.student_id = s.id GROUP BY s.id, s.name;

title: Empty intermediate result
prompt: Show how many orders have more than 100 units as big_orders. There are none in the sample, so the answer should be 0.
hints: COUNT over an empty subquery is 0.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL); UPDATE order_items SET quantity = 150 WHERE order_id = 12;

solutions: SELECT COUNT(*) AS big_orders FROM (SELECT order_id FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id HAVING SUM(quantity) > 100);

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT order_id AS big_orders FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id HAVING SUM(quantity) > 100;
SELECT COUNT(*) AS big_orders FROM order_items;

title: Fix the nested total
prompt: This should show the largest single order's units as most_units, but SQLite can't nest aggregates. Use a subquery in FROM. Fix it.
hints: Total per order inside, then MAX outside.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT MAX(units) AS most_units FROM (SELECT SUM(quantity) AS units FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id);

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT MAX(quantity) AS most_units FROM order_items;
SELECT SUM(quantity) AS most_units FROM order_items;

title: Untried pairs
prompt: A pair is one student with one course. Show how many pairs have no enrolment, as untried. Build the pairs in a subquery in FROM, then count them.
hints: CROSS JOIN, then LEFT JOIN enrolments and keep the NULLs.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring');

solutions: SELECT COUNT(*) AS untried FROM (SELECT s.id AS student_id, c.id AS course_id FROM students s CROSS JOIN courses c LEFT JOIN enrolments e ON e.student_id = s.id AND e.course_id = c.id WHERE e.id IS NULL);

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS untried FROM (SELECT s.id AS student_id, c.id AS course_id FROM students s CROSS JOIN courses c);
SELECT COUNT(*) AS untried FROM enrolments;

title: Share of pending
prompt: Show each customer_id and their percentage of pending orders as pending_pct, rounded to 1 decimal, for customers above 0%, highest first.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (14, 7, '2024-04-01', 'pending'), (15, 9, '2024-04-02', 'pending');

solutions: SELECT customer_id, pending_pct FROM (SELECT customer_id, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'pending' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 1) AS pending_pct FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id) WHERE pending_pct > 0 ORDER BY pending_pct DESC;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT customer_id, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'pending' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 1) AS pending_pct FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id ORDER BY pending_pct DESC;

SELECT customer_id, pending_pct FROM (SELECT customer_id, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'pending' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 1) AS pending_pct FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id) WHERE pending_pct > 0 ORDER BY pending_pct;
